full_text_en:
Liberia Ocean Shipping Lines Inc. v. Turkey Marti Chartering Co., Inc. — pre-litigation application for attachment of cargo

Applicant: Ocean Shipping Lines Inc., Republic of Liberia

Legal Representative: Zheng Chengxiao, Executive Director of Ocean Shipping Lines Inc.

Agent ad litem: Shen Zhenguo, lawyer at Shanghai Maritime Law Firm

Agent ad litem: Tang Yilin, lawyer at Shanghai Maritime Law Firm

Respondent: Marti Chartering Co., Inc., Republic of Turkey

On December 13, 1986, the Applicant, Ocean Shipping Lines Inc., Republic of Liberia, filed a pre-litigation preservation application with the Shanghai Maritime Court on the grounds that the Respondent, Marti Chartering Co., Inc., Republic of Turkey, failed to perform its obligations under the charter party, defaulted on the freight for the Applicant's Philippine-flag vessel M.V. GONOSAN, causing the vessel to be detained at the Port of Shanghai, People's Republic of China, and resulting in substantial economic losses to the Applicant. The Applicant requested the attachment of 1,000 metric tons of steel cargo carried by the M.V. GONOSAN until the Respondent provides a cash guarantee or bank guarantee of USD 185,000.

After accepting the application, the Shanghai Maritime Court found that on September 16, 1986, the Applicant and the Respondent entered into a voyage charter party in Copenhagen, Denmark. The parties agreed that the Applicant's vessel M.V. GONOSAN would load 5,000 metric tons and 10,130 metric tons of steel respectively at the ports of Mersin and Iskenderun, Turkey, for carriage to the port of destination — Shanghai Port, People's Republic of China. The contract stipulated that the Respondent shall pay the freight within seven days immediately after the cargo is loaded and the master issues the bill of lading, with total freight of USD 282,500 for the entire voyage, and that the Applicant has a lien on the cargo in the event of default on freight, dead freight, or demurrage. In October of the same year, the Applicant's vessel M.V. GONOSAN loaded the steel as agreed, and the master issued bills of lading with freight payable at destination and containing a clause incorporating the charter party, stating "all other conditions and exceptions as per charter party." On November 21 of the same year, after the M.V. GONOSAN arrived at Shanghai Port, the Applicant, having not received the freight, exercised a lien on 8,000 metric tons of the steel carried by the vessel, causing the vessel to be detained at Shanghai Port. After multiple rounds of negotiation, the Applicant received freight payments from the Respondent totaling USD 173,815.57, with an outstanding balance of USD 108,684.43. Additionally, due to the detention of the vessel, the Applicant incurred extra expenses for vessel maintenance, port charges, and interest losses totaling USD 94,600. To reduce losses and enable the vessel to continue operations, the Applicant filed a pre-litigation preservation application requesting that after discharge, the Shanghai Maritime Court attach 5,000 metric tons of steel to ensure the continued exercise of its lien.

After reviewing the evidence submitted by the Applicant regarding the Respondent's default on freight, the Shanghai Maritime Court ordered the Applicant to provide a guarantee of USD 50,000, and at the same time, based on the economic losses claimed by the Applicant, required the Applicant to reduce the quantity of cargo subject to the attachment application. On December 17 of the same year, the Applicant submitted a guarantee letter for USD 50,000 issued by the Shanghai Branch of The Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corporation Limited, valid for two years, to compensate for any economic losses suffered by the Respondent or other relevant parties in the event that the application was erroneous. On the same day, the Applicant amended the quantity of cargo to be attached to 1,000 metric tons of steel.

In accordance with the provision that where one party to a contract fails to perform its obligations beyond the agreed time limit, the other party is entitled to a lien on its property, and with reference to international customary practice, the Shanghai Maritime Court rendered the following ruling on December 20, 1986:

1. The pre-litigation cargo attachment application filed by the Applicant, Ocean Shipping Lines Inc., on December 13, 1986, is hereby granted.

2. 1,000 metric tons of steel discharged by the M.V. GONOSAN at Shanghai Port shall be attached.

3. The Respondent, Marti Chartering Co., Inc., must provide to the court, within 30 days from the day following receipt of this ruling, a cash guarantee of USD 185,000 or a credit guarantee of the same amount issued by a bank acceptable to the court.

After the ruling was served, the Respondent, through negotiations with the Applicant, paid part of the outstanding amount. Accordingly, on December 31, the Applicant requested the Shanghai Maritime Court to release 500 metric tons of the attached steel and continue to attach the remaining 500 metric tons.

After review, the Shanghai Maritime Court granted the Applicant's request and rendered a ruling on January 6, 1987: among the 1,000 metric tons of steel attached at Shanghai Port, 500 metric tons shall be released, and the remaining 500 metric tons shall continue to be attached.

On January 15 of the same year, given that the Respondent had fully paid off the outstanding debt, the Applicant again applied to the Shanghai Maritime Court to request the release of the attached 500 metric tons of steel.

Pursuant to the Applicant's application, the Shanghai Maritime Court granted the Applicant's request and rendered a ruling on January 16, 1987: the attachment of 500 metric tons of steel belonging to the Respondent by the Applicant shall be released; the guarantee letter for USD 50,000 issued on December 17, 1986 by the Shanghai Branch of The Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corporation Limited shall be returned.
